summary: Jann Ronis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under David F. Germano, also studying with Jeffrey Hopkins and Khenpo Sönam Tenpa, and held a post there attested in 2007.

Jared Rhoton (1941–1993) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga and completed his dissertation at Columbia University in 1985 under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

Jarl Charpentier (1884–1935) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University (PhD 1908) under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He became assistant professor at Uppsala in 1908, succeeding Johansson in 1927.
Jaroslav Průšek (1906–1980) was a sinologist who studied at the University of Prague and its Faculty of Arts from circa 1924 to 1928. His students included Karel Werner.

Jason Birch is an Indologist who studied at the University of Sydney and earned his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Oxford, SOAS University of London, and the University of Alberta.

Jason M. Wirth (born 1963) is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Kosho Itagaki. From 2014 to 2016, he held the Theiline Pigott McCone Chair in Humanities at Seattle University.

Jason Matthew McCombs is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning a B.S. at the University of Michigan, he completed his PhD under Gregory Schopen at UCLA, where he was attested as a lecturer in 2014.

Jason Neelis works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Texas at Austin and earned his PhD at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon. His posts include Wilfrid Laurier University and Ruhr University Bochum.

Jason Protass is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick and held posts as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and a Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica.

Jay Holt Valentine specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Delaware, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, where he earned his PhD under doctoral supervisor Kurtis R. Schaeffer.

Jay Jasanoff (born 1942) is a linguist and Indologist who earned his bachelor's degree at Harvard University. He held professorships at the University of California, Berkeley, Cornell University, and Harvard, including the Diebold Professorship in 1998.

Jay L. Garfield (born 1955) is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He has held faculty positions at Hampshire College, Smith College, the University of Massachusetts Amherst, the University of Melbourne, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and NUS.
Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar (1919–1974) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under M. H. Krishna at Maharaja's College, Mysore, from circa 1934 to 1938.
Jayadevbhai Mohanlal Shukla was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar and served as Reader of Sanskrit at Gujarat University.

Jayandra Soni (born 1947) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned PhDs from Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University, and held posts at the University of Marburg, University of Innsbruck, and International Association of Sanskrit Studies.

Jaś Elsner (born 1962) specializes in history, archaeology, and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge, London, Harvard, and the Courtauld Institute, he held positions at Cambridge, the Courtauld Institute, Corpus Christi College, Oxford, and the University of Oxford.
Jean Dantinne is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Étienne Lamotte and held a position as a librarian at the University of Liège.

Jean Deloche (1929–2019) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He taught at Suryavarman II School, directed the Alliance Française of Madras, and held research and associate appointments at the EFEO and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Filliozat (1906–1982) was an Indologist and historian educated at the EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He directed the French Institute of Pondicherry and the EFEO, and held chairs at the EPHE and the Collège de France.

Jean Kellens (born 1944) is an Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and linguistic scholar who studied at the University of Liège and FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg. He held academic posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, Liège, and the Collège de France.
